summary: F5 review of PR #5 at merge SHA 3185596f found that the Rust code type-checks and targeted tests pass, but the delivered changeset-state implementation is not reliable enough for the advertised multi-changeset agentic pipeline. The core validator and app validate one global event stream instead of independent changeset streams, omit from_state/initial-state enforcement, and do not enforce cost-exhaustion transitions. The app append path is non-serializable under concurrent writers, the new gate surfaces lack direct regression coverage for those edge cases, and the new workflow observes pushes to legacy main rather than the new dev default. Validation evidence: gh pr view/diff inspected, cargo check targeted crates passed, cargo test targeted crates passed, git diff --check found trailing whitespace in ADR-0114.

findings.issue: The app and CI gate pass the entire global changeset-event-log into validate_monotonic_event_log as one stream. The validator keeps a single last_advancing_ordinal and terminal_state, with no grouping by changeset_id. That makes the second valid changeset fail after the first advances or terminates: e.g. cs1 opened->working followed by cs2 opened is treated as a backwards transition; cs1 produced followed by any terminal row for cs2 is treated as MultipleTerminalStates. ADR-0110 says the monotonic sequence is per changeset, so this implementation cannot reliably support more than one changeset in the canonical log.
findings.remediation: Group events by changeset_id before validation. In the app, validate only the target changeset's existing rows plus the candidate, then write the global log after the per-changeset check passes. In the gate, iterate all changeset groups and report the failing changeset_id. Add regression tests with two interleaved valid changesets, two independent terminal states, and one invalid changeset among valid neighbors.

findings.issue: The row contract says from_state is None only on the first Opened row and subsequent rows must carry the preceding to_state, but validate_monotonic_event_log never enforces either rule. It accepts a first row at an arbitrary later state, accepts missing from_state on non-first rows, and accepts a from_state that does not match the previous event. This weakens the state-machine contract into an ordinal-only check and lets malformed histories pass the new fitness lane.
findings.remediation: Extend the validator to require first row to_state == Opened and from_state == None; for every subsequent advancing or terminal row, require from_state == previous.to_state except for explicitly modeled skip rules. Add tests for wrong first state, missing non-first from_state, mismatched from_state, and valid skip rows.

findings.issue: CostBudget::is_exhausted exists and the docs say an exhausted axis must force cost_exhausted, but the validator never calls is_exhausted and the app parser accepts any numeric usd_remaining, including negative values. A log can continue to reviewed/produced with usd_remaining < 0 and still pass monotonicity and enum-closed gates as long as ordinals increase. The unit tests only verify the helper returns true for zero; they do not test that exhausted budgets are rejected unless the transition is CostExhausted.
findings.remediation: Make budget exhaustion part of the state validator: if any event's remaining budget is exhausted, the same row must be to_state == CostExhausted and no later rows may exist. Reject negative budget values unless they are deliberately allowed and documented. Add positive/negative validator tests for each budget axis.

findings.issue: Append is read-parse-push-validate-write with no interprocess lock or compare-and-swap. Atomic rename prevents torn writes, but it does not serialize two writers that both read the same old log and then write competing N+1 versions. The temp path is also fixed as path.with_extension("json.tmp"), so concurrent writers can overwrite the same temp file before either rename. Under the webhook/orchestrator model introduced by the PR, this can silently lose valid events or rename another writer's payload.
findings.remediation: Protect the entire read/validate/write critical section with a lock file or switch to an append-only JSONL/event-store shape with atomic append/CAS semantics. Use unique temp paths per process if retaining whole-file writes. Add a regression test that spawns multiple appends against the same log and asserts all distinct events survive.

findings.issue: Test coverage is too shallow for the new CI surfaces. The kernel has unit tests for simple monotonic branches and the app has one append-to-empty-log round trip, but the newly added oya gate validate changeset-state-* dispatchers have no direct integration tests for malformed logs, invalid enum rows, non-empty success, missing/empty log policy, or multi-changeset logs. The current tests therefore pass while the per-changeset grouping, from_state-chain, cost-exhaustion, and concurrent-append defects remain uncovered.
findings.remediation: Add gate_cli integration tests that invoke both new gate commands against fixture logs: valid multi-changeset, invalid enum, backwards transition within one changeset, missing/empty log with explicit expected policy, malformed event shape, and exhausted-budget cases. Add app-level concurrency and duplicate-dedup tests.

findings.issue: The new changeset-state workflow is registered as active per-pr quality infrastructure, but its push trigger is still branches: [main] while PR #5 moves the protected/default shared branch to dev. Pull requests will run it, but post-merge pushes to dev will not. That leaves the newly introduced event-log lanes unobserved on the branch where the pipeline actually advances, which is a reliability gap for a state log that is intended to be mutated after merge.
findings.remediation: Change the push trigger to branches: [dev] (or [dev, staging, production] if these lanes are expected to observe promotion refs). Add a lightweight workflow-trigger regression or repository policy check that rejects new per-pr workflows whose push branches do not include the configured default/protected branch.

findings.issue: git diff --check on the PR reports trailing whitespace on the staged canary flow lines. This is not functionally dangerous, but it indicates the formatting gate did not cover Markdown whitespace in a PR that otherwise adds a large amount of process-critical documentation.
findings.remediation: Trim the trailing spaces and add a doc whitespace check, or include Markdown in the existing formatting/static checks so future ADR-only portions of mixed PRs get the same hygiene coverage as Rust.
